title: Hardwood vs Laminate Flooring: Which Is Worth It in Edmonds?
meta: Hardwood vs laminate in Edmonds: $3.25 vs $2.50 per sq ft labor, but hardwood refinishes for decades and laminate does not. Where each wins. Wills Flooring.

blocks.lead: Hardwood is worth it in an Edmonds home you plan to keep or sell at full value: it costs $0.75 more per sq ft to install than laminate, but it can be refinished for 50 years and buyers in the Bowl and Seaview pay for it. Laminate is the better call for a rental, a basement or a budget that has to cover the whole house at once.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring installs hardwood at $3.25 per sq ft for labor and laminate at $2.50, both with a 500 sq ft minimum. Material is quoted separately at the free estimate, and that is where the real gap between the two shows up.

blocks.html: A common version of this question in Edmonds sounds like: we bought a 1960s rambler in Seaview, the carpet has to go, and laminate looks fine in the samples, so why would we pay more for wood? It is a fair question, and laminate has gotten a lot better. The answer depends on three things: how long you will own the house, what the room is, and what the next buyer in your neighborhood expects. This post puts real numbers and Edmonds-specific realities on each.

blocks.text: What the two really cost over 25 years

items.title: Hardwood, 900 sq ft main floor
items.text: Install labor: 900 × $3.25 = $2,925, plus material. Around year 12 you screen and recoat at $1.99 per sq ft: $1,791. Around year 25 a full sand and refinish at $3.99: $3,591. The floor is still original wood and still adding value.

items.title: Laminate, same 900 sq ft
items.text: Install labor: 900 × $2.50 = $2,250, plus material. Nothing can be renewed, so by year 15 to 20 the worn kitchen path and a swollen edge at the dishwasher mean a second full install: another $2,250 in labor plus new material and tear-out.

items.title: The crossover
items.text: Laminate wins on day one by $675 in labor and usually more in material. Hardwood wins the moment laminate is replaced once. If you will own the Edmonds house for more than about 12 years, wood is the cheaper floor over its life.

items.title: Resale changes the math again
items.text: Buyers touring a Bowl or Seaview home expect hardwood on the main floor. Laminate in the listing photos reads as a project to redo. That does not show up on an invoice, but it shows up on the offer.

blocks.note: For laminate, use the $2.50 rate on our laminate installation page. Both carry the 500 sq ft minimum.

a.title: Choose wood when
items: It is the main living floor of a house you will keep or sell at full value
The home is a 1950s to 70s rambler with original character worth matching

b.title: Choose laminate when
items: It is a rental, a basement or a kids' playroom
The whole house needs floors on one budget, now
You want maximum scratch resistance for dogs and expect to replace it in 15 years
The subfloor is a slab and you want a floating floor without glue
The house is a short-term flip in a price band where buyers will not pay for wood

blocks.text: Edmonds realities that tilt the decision

items.text: Homes in the Bowl and along the bluff live in salt air and steady humidity. Both floors need acclimation, but laminate's fiberboard core is the one that swells for good if the humidity swings hard. Engineered hardwood is the most stable option near the water.

Seaview, Westgate and Perrinville ramblers often have oak in the living room and carpet in the bedrooms. Matching new hardwood into the old is straightforward for us; laminate next to real oak never quite passes.
A lot of Edmonds buyers are moving from bigger Eastside homes and expect the same finishes. Hardwood on the main floor of a downsizing condo or rambler is close to required at that price point.
Slab lower levels in Esperance and along the ravines are where laminate or vinyl plank make sense. Solid hardwood does not belong below grade at all.

blocks.text: When hardwood is not worth it, honestly

items.html: You will sell within three years and the neighborhood does not command it. If comparable Edmonds listings show laminate and sell fine, you will not recover the difference.
The room gets wet regularly. Mudrooms, laundry rooms and bathrooms are not hardwood rooms. Frankly they are not laminate rooms either; vinyl plank is the right answer there.
The subfloor needs a lot of work. Hardwood wants a flat, dry, solid subfloor. If the crawlspace is damp or the plywood is soft, spend on that first; the floor choice comes second.
It is a rental with turnover every year or two. Laminate takes tenant abuse and can be replaced a room at a time without matching anything.

blocks.title: The most common mistake we see:
blocks.text: Choosing laminate for the main floor of a nice Edmonds home to save on labor, then discovering the material savings were small once a good underlayment and quality plank were priced. Get both quotes with material at the same estimate before deciding. We bring samples of each.
Decide it properly: a short checklist

items: Write down how many years you expect to own the house. Under 5, lean laminate; over 12, lean hardwood.
Check three recent Edmonds listings in your price band and note what floors they show.
Get both options quoted with material, underlayment and removal at the same visit.
Ask whether the subfloor is plywood or slab and whether it is dry enough for either floor.
Decide room by room. Hardwood in living areas plus vinyl plank in wet rooms is the usual Edmonds answer.
Confirm the 1-year workmanship warranty and the manufacturer's finish warranty on whichever you choose.

faq.q: Is laminate cheaper than hardwood to install?
faq.a: Yes. Wills Flooring installs laminate at $2.50 per sq ft and hardwood at $3.25, so labor on a 900 sq ft floor differs by $675. Material widens the gap, since quality hardwood costs more per box than laminate. Over 25 years, though, laminate is usually replaced once, and hardwood is refinished instead.

faq.q: Does laminate hurt resale value in Edmonds?
faq.a: In the Bowl, Seaview and near downtown, buyers expect hardwood in main living areas and often read laminate as a future project. In basements, rentals and lower-priced homes it is neutral. Check what recent listings in your price band show before deciding.

faq.q: Which holds up better to dogs, hardwood or laminate?
faq.a: Laminate's surface resists claw scratches better day to day. Hardwood shows scratches sooner, but they sand out during a refinish, while a chipped laminate plank can only be replaced. For a dog household that plans to stay, a hard species like white oak with a matte finish is the better long-term floor.

No. The surface is a printed photo under a wear layer, with no real wood to sand. Once it is worn or chipped, the plank is replaced. Hardwood, whether solid or engineered with a thick wear layer, can be sanded and refinished multiple times over its life.

faq.q: Is engineered hardwood a good middle option?
faq.a: Often the best one in Edmonds. It installs at the same $3.25 per sq ft as solid, is more stable in waterfront humidity, works over concrete and radiant heat, and can still be refinished if the wear layer is 3 mm or thicker. It looks and sounds like solid wood because the top layer is solid wood.

faq.q: How long does each floor last?
faq.a: Hardwood lasts 50 to 100 years with a recoat every decade or so and a full refinish every 20 to 25. Laminate lasts 15 to 25 years depending on quality and traffic, then is replaced. That difference is the core of why hardwood is cheaper over a long ownership.
